title: AI Interpretation Scorecards for Hospital Leaders
summary: Build a hospital AI interpretation scorecard for access, quality, patient understanding, reliability, cost, risk, and leadership decisions.
body_markdown:
###


A hospital scorecard should measure access, communication quality, patient understanding, operational reliability, cost, and unresolved risk within a defined United States care setting. Each rate should show its denominator, reporting period, included languages, and data source so leaders can interpret the result without the surrounding report.


###


No. In an Opalite deployment, Guardian findings should be reported separately from errors confirmed through the hospital’s review process. The scorecard should show the number of encounters reviewed, findings generated, findings confirmed, severity, resolution status, and limits of the review sample.


###


Hospitals should compare matched United States encounter groups by language, department, clinical task, shift, and complexity when the data support that design. Report unmatched cases separately because different patient needs and encounter types can make a hospital-wide comparison misleading.


###


No. A hospital financial scorecard should also report total program cost, cost per completed encounter, setup and integration costs, quality-review work, complementary human interpretation, and the volume of patients served. Opalite does not charge for hold or silent time, but comparisons should still use each vendor’s full contract terms.


###


The review cadence should follow the hospital’s risk, volume, and decision calendar rather than a universal schedule. Operational owners can monitor failures and high-severity concerns promptly, while governance leaders can review trends, overdue actions, budget questions, and expansion decisions on a defined recurring cadence.
